title: Quarterly Lynx: personal metrics & guardrails (draft)
body:
Context:
This is my personal quarterly note — a small, pragmatic set of metrics and rituals I can actually keep up with. Not an org OKR, not a performance review doc, just a lightweight accountability layer. Drafting this here because I want something I can iterate on weekly and carry forward into next quarter without the noise.

Top-level intent: increase reliable output while protecting deep work and mental bandwidth. Tradeoffs: fewer ambiguous goals, more measurable habits.

Primary outcome metrics (one-line targets):
- Deep work hours: 12+ hours/week (focused, single-task blocks >= 45m).
- Meaningful PRs merged: 6+ substantial PRs / month (feature or infra, not docs).
- Merge lead time: median <= 24h for reviews when not on PTO or blocked.
- Unplanned incidents (user-impacting): 0 per quarter (target), accept 1 as tolerance.
- Learning cycles: 1 small experiment per month (optimizations, quantization test, perf tweak).

Why these?
- Deep work hours protect quality and unblock larger features.
- PRs + lead time measure my throughput and collaboration hygiene.
- Incidents track reliability responsibility and on-call floor.
- Monthly experiments keep me from stagnating.

Leading indicators / habits (actions I will actually track):
- Morning 90 block: 3x week minimum (calendar blocked 9:00–10:30 Tue/Thu + one flexible).
- No-meeting Friday afternoon (two-hour coding window) — carry it forward unless critical.
- Daily triage note (5–10 minutes): one line of progress, blockers, experiment note.
- Weekly write-up (Fri): 6–8 bullet check-in summarizing outcome metrics and one explicit ask for feedback.

Quick measurement plan (lightweight):
- Deep work: manual tally on Monday snapshot (not obsessed).
- PRs merged: GitHub query + manual tag in weekly note.
- Lead time: sample week every 2 weeks, record median.
- Incidents: link to postmortem or Slack thread.

Quarterly retrospective (previous quarter highlights & lowlights):
- Wins: landed the L1 KV cache improvement (reduced 95p latency on small seqs), ran a small quantization A/B that saved ~6% token-cost on internal evals.
- Misses: allowed calendar creep, failed to ship two small infra refactors due to context switching.
- Learning: strict meeting hygiene matters more than vague "time saved" promises.

Primary hypotheses to test this quarter:
1) Reserving 3x 90m deep blocks/week will increase merge throughput by 25% (fewer interruptions -> larger contiguous work -> faster PR closures).
2) A weekly 6-bullet update to a small list of reviewers will reduce lead time by making review context explicit.
3) Adding a tiny pre-PR checklist (tests + perf expectations + reviewers suggested) will reduce rework at review time.

Fail modes I should watch for:
- Over-optimizing metrics (hitting PR count by slicing work into small PRs). Guardrail: prefer larger, meaningful PRs; annotate size and impact in weekly note.
- Burnout: if deep work hours rise but mood and energy fall, pause and recalibrate.
- Visibility tax: spending too much time producing the weekly artifact instead of doing the work. Keep the weekly note to 6 bullets.

Weekly check-in template (copy into Friday note):
- Week ending: YYYY-MM-DD
- Deep hours: X (target 12+)
- PRs merged: N (names/links)
- Median lead time sample: Y hours
- Incidents: list or none
- Experiment status: quick result or next step
- One ask for feedback (explicit)

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Block Tue/Thu 9:00–10:30 and Fri 15:00–17:00 on calendar; mark as tentative.
- Add pre-PR checklist as a GitHub issue template (small PR draft). Linked ticket: JIRA-ENG-3421.
- Send first weekly check-in next Friday to Aisha & Ethan.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How strict should I be about counting meetings that are "working sessions"? If pair-programming with a teammate counts as deep work, treat as 50% credit.
- Is the 12h deep-work bar realistic given meetings + oncall? If not, scale to 9h.
- If lead time stays >48h, escalate review expectations on Tuesday sync.

References and quick links:
- Confluence draft for KV cache notes: CONFLUENCE-7892
- Related ticketing: JIRA-ENG-3421 (pre-PR checklist)
- Slack thread where Aisha gave feedback: slack://thread/C12345

Triage log (scratch; remove later):
- 2025-09-12: initial sketch, drafted metrics, added morning 90 idea.
- 2025-09-19: blocked by meetings — adjusted expectation to 9h if needed.
- 2025-09-26: implemented PR template draft; need to sync with Ethan.

This is intentionally lean. Revisit after 4 weeks and decide whether to keep, shelve, or escalate to a broader personal development doc.

---
Small stylistic rule: keep weekly note to 6 bullets. If I find myself writing paragraphs every week, I'm using it as therapy instead of feedback.

End.
